channel.title: Cities & Climate Learning Lab — Current Conversations
channel.description: Recent conversations connected to the lab research themes.

item.title: Engaging urban SMEs in net-zero transitions to mitigate climate change: Navigating multi-level governance challenges
item.description: Drawing on interviews and policy documents, the study considers how multi-level governance arrangements influence climate action among small and medium-sized enterprises in Melbourne.

item.title: Local capacity building and policy evaluation in climate and environmental governance
item.description: The paper examines how local capacity building and policy evaluation shape climate and environmental governance, using Mexico City as a case through which to discuss urban transformation.

item.title: Assessing intersectional inequities in climate finance across Atlantic Canada
item.description: The study examines uneven access to government and philanthropic climate finance in Atlantic Canada, with a primary case study in Nova Scotia.

item.title: Evaluating ERA5-Land air temperature and dew point biases in built-up environments in the UK
item.description: The study evaluates temperature and dew-point biases in ERA5-Land data across built-up UK environments and considers how those biases propagate into urban climate applications.

item.title: Social Impacts of the Green Transition: Prospective Environmental (In)Justice in Europe's Peripheries
item.description: Using six case studies, the article considers prospective environmental injustice associated with decarbonisation, critical minerals, regional strategies and gaps between workforce and socio-ecological policy.

item.title: From pilot to paradigm: a call for entrepreneurial strategies to scale up the implementation of nature-based solutions
item.description: The article asks how cities can move nature-based solutions beyond isolated pilots and discusses more proactive implementation strategies and their potential co-benefits.

item.title: Multi-layered Urban Forests: can a City be dense and green?
item.description: The paper discusses how urban density and layered urban forest design can be considered together rather than treated as mutually exclusive planning goals.

item.title: July breaks drought and heat records in France: The issue of water is becoming absolutely critical
item.description: Le Monde reports on French heat and drought records and the resulting pressure on water systems, communities and public authorities.

item.title: This summer isn't breaking heat records yet. Wait until El Nino kicks in, scientists say
item.description: Associated Press reports scientists' assessment of the interaction between long-term warming, a strengthening El Nino and extreme heat affecting cities and regions.

item.title: Beating the Heat Together: City Diplomacy and the Global Mobilization against Extreme Heat
item.description: UNEP's event page frames extreme heat as a topic for city diplomacy and shared urban learning among municipal and international actors.

item.title: Data Portal for Cities
item.description: The platform provides preliminary city emissions data and export functions intended to help local governments build inventories and set priorities.

item.title: Building Communities Strong in British Columbia with 54 new infrastructure projects
item.description: The federal announcement describes funding for local infrastructure projects in British Columbia through arrangements involving Canada, the province, UBCM and local governments.

item.title: Planning data-driven climate adaptation actions
item.description: The Covenant of Mayors describes a platform offering comparable Earth-observation data intended to support adaptation planning across European cities.

item.title: COOLCITY Index.eu
item.description: The platform offers comparable urban climate and environmental indicators intended to support adaptation prioritisation across European cities.

item.title: Local Records Data Viewer
item.description: The viewer provides filterable daily temperature records for US cities using open data from NOAA regional climate centres.

item.title: Preparing the maritime workforce for the twin transition: skill priorities and educational needs
item.description: The study investigates skill priorities and education needs created by the maritime sector's linked decarbonisation and digital transitions.

item.title: Mayor Owens Announces Adoption of Inaugural Climate Action Plan
item.description: The City of Syracuse announced adoption of its first community and municipal climate action plan, covering resilience, energy, mobility, education, heat and flooding.

item.title: From Observation to Decision: An Introduction to Synthesis by Berkeley Earth
item.description: Berkeley Earth introduces a platform connecting historical observations with bias-corrected climate projections at local scale for cities and countries.

item.title: Reuters Climate Monitor
item.description: Copernicus describes a Reuters interactive that compares current temperatures with historical averages and includes city-oriented views.

item.title: July 4th: The Hottest Month Is Getting Hotter After 250 Years of Climate Change
item.description: Climate Central presents city-level July temperature trends, downloadable data and methodology for more than 240 US cities.

item.title: Mayors from around the world unite in call for sustainable urban data centres
item.description: C40 describes a pact through which participating mayors seek to shape urban data-centre growth around energy, water, land, cost and community concerns.

item.title: The UrbClim model
item.description: The UrbClim site describes a city-scale climate model offering high-resolution outputs for heat and related variables across historical and future periods.

item.title: Why the Right to Housing is the Key to Climate Survival
item.description: C40 commentary links housing rights, construction, affordability and climate resilience and points to a related white paper developed with The Shift.

item.title: How Austin uses AI to address tree canopies
item.description: Axios reports on Austin's use of aerial, weather and socioeconomic data to examine tree-canopy and shade disparities.

item.title: Local Government Climate Action Program has not been renewed
item.description: UBCM reports that a provincial programme used by local governments for climate staffing, planning and implementation was not renewed in the 2026/27 service plan.
